output.brief: The wrong expiry was not an operator error. Printer records show no overrides on any of the 47 Veltranol jobs. Until 3 Oct the system sent a 24-month shelf life. From 4 Oct it sent 36 months, on Line 3 nights and on two Line 1 day jobs run by permanent staff. The ERP shows Regulatory Affairs entered 36 months on 3 Oct, but only valid from 1 Mar 2027, and the 24-month value is still the one in effect. Somehow the future value reached the printers, which contradicts the vendor's claim that it can't. I haven't confirmed how, so check the PackBridge configuration. Firmware and agency staff fit the timing poorly. Jobs after the firmware change were fine, and the agency staff's first jobs were correct. Drop the warnings and removals: they punish the wrong party and leave the fault in place. Reset the Veltranol shelf-life record, hold all Veltranol lots packed since 4 Oct, including the two Line 1 lots in the warehouse, and add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at every setup. Also inspect the two other products with future-dated edits (HX-15-30, MR-05-14). Keep the camera check on. It only compares print to job data, so it needs that second check alongside it. Confidence is fairly high on cause, lower on the exact mechanism and on other products.
